t: 3579. Minimum Steps to Convert String with Operations — Editorial
o:
## Understanding the problem
Given equal-length `word1`, `word2`, cut `word1` into contiguous pieces; per piece you may do one replace (one index), one swap (two indices), one reverse (whole piece), each index usable once per operation type. Minimize total operations.

Example 1 splits `abcdf` into `ab`,`c`,`df`: reversing `ab` (1 op) then replacing `a→d` (1 op), plus two replaces on `df` = 4. Example 3 shows one reverse + one swap on the whole string = 2.

With n ≤ 100, an O(n³) interval DP over substring costs plus a second DP over cut positions fits easily.
k: For a segment, the only useful whole-segment moves are: reverse (fixes both mirrored ends), swap+reverse (fixes one mirrored end), or replacing mismatched ends individually.
Interval DP computes the cheapest transformation of every substring; a knapsack-style DP over cut points combines segments.
Any segment can always be finished by replacing mismatched characters one-by-one, so a valid finite cost always exists.

a.i: Define dp[i][j] = min operations to turn word1[i..j] into word2[i..j] treating it as one segment. Either split at k (costs add), or use whole-segment operations on the two boundary characters: if both ends already match, recurse inward free; if crossed matches (s[i]==t[j] and s[j]==t[i]) one reverse suffices; if one crossed match exists, swap+reverse (2 ops) fixes both ends. Then g[j] = min over i of g[i-1] + dp[i][j] picks the best partition.
s: Base: dp[i][i] = 0 if characters equal else 1.
Fill dp by increasing length using split, both-match, reverse, and swap+reverse transitions.
Run g over prefixes to choose optimal segmentation.
a.t: O(n³) — O(n²) intervals, O(n) splits each; n ≤ 100 so ~10⁶ work.

w: The interval DP is the interview answer; brute-force per-segment enumeration is exponential and not viable. Pitfalls: forgetting the swap+reverse (2-op) case, mishandling length-2 inner segments (inner = 0), and off-by-one in the segmentation DP. Follow-up: reconstruct the actual segmentation and operations.
